prompt_before:
You are given a sequence of integers A = (A_1, A_2, A_3).
Let B = (B_1, B_2, B_3) be any permutation related of A.
Determine whether it is possible that B_1 \times B_2 = B_3.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
A_1 A_2 A_3
Output
If it is possible that B_1 \times B_2 = B_3, print Yes; otherwise, print No.
Constraints
- All input values are integers.
- 1 \le A_1, A_2, A_3 \le 100

candidates.question: Must the permutation B be a rearrangement of all three elements of A, or can it reuse an element more than once or omit some elements?
candidates.answer: Yes, B must be a strict permutation of A, containing exactly the same three elements with their order rearranged. You cannot reuse, omit, or add elements.
